title: Critical TechWorks is a captive BMW joint venture and therefore not addressable
content:
Critical TechWorks appears in the workbook as a captive BMW joint venture, and the screen's verdict is that it is not addressable. Its tool column is recorded as n/a — no platform relationship was found to assess, which is consistent with a captive: its technology choices follow the parent's programme rather than a market position it sells.

Captivity is a harder disqualifier than any of the fit criteria, because it removes the buyer rather than the fit. The partner thesis needs a firm that can decide to carry a new layer into its own client engagements. A joint venture built to serve one owner has no such client engagements of its own, so there is no place for a partnership to attach even if the technical argument landed perfectly.

This is worth recording rather than simply dropping, because captives are easy to mistake for scaled engineering firms from headcount and job postings alone. The category — captive subsidiary or joint venture — is the reusable screen, and it recurs in the workbook with automotive parents in particular.
